<action type="say">
Here’s exactly how to handle this with whichever airline or site you used.

1) What to have ready before you contact them
- Your confirmation code: BK-DL7710-20260925  
- Your full name as on the ticket: Aisha Nkrumah  
- Your approximate original trip: round trip to Boston, late September 2026, return a few days after outbound  
- Your request:  
  - Change: outbound only  
  - New outbound date: 2026-09-28  
  - Time preference: morning departure  
- Be prepared that:
  - There may be a change fee, and  
  - You may pay or receive a fare difference.

2) Phone script (you can read or paraphrase)
“Hi, my name is Aisha Nkrumah. I have a round-trip booking to Boston and I’d like to change just my outbound flight.

My confirmation code is BK-DL7710-20260925, and my last name is spelled N-K-R-U-M-A-H.

I want to keep my existing return flight exactly as it is. I only need to move the outbound flight to the morning of September 28, 2026. Could you please search for morning flights on 2026-09-28 and tell me what options are available, including any change fees and fare differences?

Again, I do not want to cancel the whole booking — I just want to change the outbound and keep the return as is.”

If they propose options, you can say:
“Which of those options has the lowest total extra cost? And can you confirm the exact new departure and arrival times, plus any fees and fare difference, before you make the change?”

Before ending the call:
“Please confirm the final itinerary and costs:  
- New outbound flight number, date, and times  
- That my return flight is unchanged  
- Total I was charged or refunded  
- That my confirmation code is still [repeat code] or what the new one is.”

3) Chat message template (website/app chat)
You can paste something like:

“Hi, I’d like help changing part of an existing booking.

Name: Aisha Nkrumah  
Confirmation code: BK-DL7710-20260925  

This is a round trip to Boston. I want to keep my return flight exactly as it is and only change the outbound. Please move my outbound flight to the morning of 2026-09-28. 

Could you:
1) Confirm that it’s possible to change only the outbound and keep the return,  
2) Show me the available morning options on 2026-09-28, and  
3) Tell me the total cost, including any change fees and fare difference, before you make any changes?

Please proceed only after I confirm which new outbound flight I want. And please confirm that the return flight remains unchanged after the change.”

4) Email template (if you must email)
Subject: Request to Change Outbound Flight Only – Confirmation BK-DL7710-20260925

Body:

“Dear Customer Support,

I am writing to request a change to the outbound portion of my round-trip booking.

Name: Aisha Nkrumah  
Confirmation code: BK-DL7710-20260925  

Trip details (approximate): Round trip to Boston in late September 2026, with the return a few days after the outbound.

I would like to:
- Change ONLY the outbound flight to the morning of 2026-09-28  
- Keep the existing return flight exactly as it is

Please:
1. Confirm whether it is possible to change only the outbound leg and keep the return unchanged.  
2. Provide me with available outbound flight options on the morning of 2026-09-28.  
3. Inform me of any change fees and fare differences associated with each option.  
4. Do not proceed with any changes until I reply confirming my preferred option.

In your reply, please clearly confirm:
- The selected new outbound flight number, date, and times  
- That my return flight remains unchanged  
- The total amount charged or refunded, and the updated confirmation code if it changes.

Thank you for your assistance.

Sincerely,  
Aisha Nkrumah”

5) Key phrases to use/avoid
- Always say clearly: “Change ONLY the outbound; keep the return as is.”  
- Ask: “Please confirm any change fees and fare differences before you finalize the change.”  
- Avoid saying “cancel my outbound” unless you fully understand whether that will also affect your return.

If you’d like, you can paste me what they reply with (from chat or email), and I can help you decide which option to accept or how to respond. </action>
